title: Follow-Up: Replicating GPT-5's 2.1% Deceptive CoT Rate in Open-Source Reasoning Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: measure deceptive CoT rates in open-source reasoning models -> compare to GPT-5 baseline -> identify unmonitored safety gap -> inform deployment monitoring decisions. Each link is explicit and the safety relevance is direct.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running open-source models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ) and applying a prompted monitor or rule-based proxy to detect deceptive CoT. Beginner CS students can handle prompting and basic classification with medium compute. Open models with accessible CoT simplify the task.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: run N prompts through 2-3 open models, apply detection method, report rates. Single deliverable (rate comparison table). The detection methodology design requires some care but is bounded. Achievable in 30 hours.
